description: Follow Bedford's river engineering to a brewer's art collection and the Corn Exchange's wartime broadcasts before finishing with John Bunyan.
short_description: An iron bridge, collected art, Glenn Miller memories and a literary meal.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
recommended_age: Recommended 10+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A westbound route from the Embankment through the cultural quarter to Midland Road, ending near Bedford station.

before_you_go.terrain: Surfaced Embankment paths, bridge approaches and town-centre paving through Bedford’s cultural quarter.
before_you_go.hills: Flat apart from the gentle suspension-bridge approaches.
before_you_go.steps: No building entry or steps are required for the outdoor checkpoints.
before_you_go.accessibility: The riverside and central route is broadly step-free, though flooding, events and temporary works can cause diversions.
before_you_go.toilets: Check The Higgins, council and shopping-area facility listings and opening times before starting.
before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable shoes with grip are useful beside the river after wet weather.
before_you_go.dogs: Dogs can join the outdoor walk on a lead; check the Pilgrim’s Progress venue policy before entering.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally suitable on surfaced paths and pavements, with gentle bridge gradients.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Begin at the slender iron crossing built by the town's great Victorian foundry.
stops.Hint_1: Head to the Embankment east of the town centre.
stops.Hint_2: Find the pedestrian suspension bridge over the Great Ouse.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Bedford Suspension Bridge opened in 1888. It was designed by John J. Webster and made by Bedford's Britannia Iron Works.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the riverbank, find the chains, towers and deck and decide which part appears to carry the load.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find a museum where a brewer's home and art collection grew into the town's shared memory.
stops.Hint_1: Walk west along the river and turn into Castle Lane.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the museum complex behind the historic frontage.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The Higgins brings together Bedford Museum and the Cecil Higgins Art Gallery. Higgins, a local brewer, left his home and art collection to the town, and the gallery opened in 1949.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From outside, identify two different building periods or materials in the museum complex.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find the hall where wartime radio travelled nationwide and an American bandleader played.
stops.Hint_1: Continue west to Saint Paul's Square.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the large civic hall facing the square.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Bedford Corn Exchange opened in 1874. During the Second World War the BBC used Bedford for broadcasts, and Glenn Miller and his orchestra performed from the Corn Exchange in 1944.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Find one date, plaque or musical reference visible from the public square.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Finish with the journey of Christian, named for the Bedford writer whose pilgrim crossed the world in print.
stops.Hint_2: Find the food-serving pub and hotel named after John Bunyan's book.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! The pub is named after The Pilgrim's Progress, written by John Bunyan, who lived most of his life in and around Bedford in the seventeenth century. Check today's hours before stopping for food or a drink.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From outside, find a book, pilgrim or journey motif in the signage.
